issues.detail: The Greek 'αναστας' (anas-tas) means 'arising' or 'getting up', but the Vietnamese 'chạy đến' means 'running to'. The Greek does not specify running.

The Greek 'μονα' (mona) refers to the linen cloths being alone/only; the Vietnamese 'một mình' is used here to describe the cloth, but 'môna' in this context emphasizes that there was nothing else there.
